name: Janabai
bio: Janabai (Jani Bai) is a Marathi woman saint-poet of the 14th century, remembered as a maidservant in the household of Namdev and a devotee of Vithoba of Pandharpur.
Her songs (abhangs) draw on the labours of household life, as in the grinding-mill hymn. Macnicol's Psalms of Maratha Saints (1919) gives three of them.

poems.title: Pundlik
poems.author: Janabai
poems.text:
To holy Pundlik give
The highest place.
Sages and saints he saved, —
Saved by his grace.

Thou, standing on the brick,
That grace give me,
Who, Pundlik, clasp thy feet,
So lowlily.

poems.title: Grinding
poems.author: Janabai
poems.text:
Dispassion's mill, with earnest mind,
Lo, here grind I, —
While for a handle faith I find
To turn it by.

A handful of past deeds I deem
Grist for the mill,
And grind in the one Soul supreme
My good or ill.

All outward form to dust is ground,
All eyes can see,
For 'tis the Lord himself, I've found,
Who grinds for me.

Strange that this god should come and sit.
His servant nigh;
For I've had nought to do with it,
Says Janabai.

poems.title: The Besetting God
poems.author: Janabai
poems.text:
Of God my meat and drink I make,
God is the bed on which I lie.
God is whate'er I give or take;
God's constant fellowship have I
For God is here and God is there, —
No place that empty is of him.
Yea, lady Vitha, I declare,
I fill the world up to the brim.
